full_text: Readers may be familiar with the fundamental changes that took place in the Roman world as it converted from paganism  to Christianity. As Christianity spread throughout Europe, it brought with it a number of societal changes, including a shift towards more monogamous family structures and the prohibition of practices like infanticide and abortion. In "The Fall of the Roman Empire" (1964), Edward Gibbon argues that the adoption of Christianity by the Roman Empire contributed to its downfall. Gibbon believed that the Christian movement's rejection of Roman paganism and its rigid moral codes weakened the empire's values and moral fiber. He also believed that Christianity's dogmatic teachings stifled intellectual curiosity and scientific inquiry, which further contributed to the decline of the empire. Some
